claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl feedstock with a particle size range of 15–45 μm is typically used in HVAF deposition.
Standard HVAF-i7 parameters with 15–45 μm feedstock produce coatings of acceptable quality.
Standard HVAF-i7 parameters with 15–45 μm feedstock produce inadequate coating thickness.
Increasing particle velocity on the HVAF-i7 system will increase the deposition efficiency of FeCoNiCrAl.
Setting the HVAF-i7 spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase the deposition efficiency of FeCoNiCrAl.
The proposed increase in deposition efficiency will overcome the current coating-thickness limitation.
Higher particle velocity increases particle kinetic energy.
Higher particle kinetic energy promotes more effective particle impingement.
Higher particle kinetic energy improves splat formation and particle flattening upon impact.
More efficient particle flattening improves coating adhesion.
Increased particle kinetic energy reduces in-flight oxidation.
Improved adhesion and reduced in-flight oxidation collectively produce a thicker bond coat.
The adjusted parameters will produce a thicker bond coat than the standard HVAF-i7 baseline.
The adjusted parameters will produce a more adherent bond coat with minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention will meet coating-performance requirements in internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The intervention should remain effective with similar feedstock compositions and the same HVAF-i7 hardware.
Significant changes in feedstock size or torch design may alter the intervention's effectiveness.
Prior MCrAlY and HVAF-M3 studies indicate that the proposed parameter changes may improve deposition.
